title: JLI Global Essay Competition
verdict: Row is accurate and well-maintained. No correction proposed.
confirmed: cycle_status='closed' matches the live page ('Registration for the 2026 Global Essay Prize is now closed'); maximum_age=19 and cost=0.00 both correct; description already captures the ten subject categories and the late-fee structure.
one_addition_worth_making: 'Junior contestants may answer any question from any category, and will be judged separately, against their age peers, within each category.' The existing description does not mention a Junior division exists — worth adding, since it changes who this is appropriate for at the younger end of ORYN's 14-18 band.
judging_panel_verbatim: 'judged by a panel of senior academics drawn from leading universities including Oxford, Cambridge, Harvard, Princeton, and Stanford, under the leadership of the Chairman of Examiners, Prof. Terence Kealey.'
why_checked: Product-derived gap analysis (CR1-152) found Politics/Law/History thin (3/0/2). JLI covers all three plus Philosophy, Psychology, Public Policy, International Relations, Theology, Economics, Science & Technology — the single broadest-subject-coverage row possible. Worth confirming it was healthy before looking elsewhere.
next_cycle: NOT STATED — no 2027 page found yet. Re-check per the existing row's own cadence.

entry_mechanism_verbatim: 'Each student who is taking the exam must register for the current year's USABO... Students may only access the Student Resource Center (SRC) after their school's $125 registration fee has been received and the school's or Institution's account has been activated.'
school_gate_note: A student cannot register without a HOST SCHOOL registering and paying first. 'A student may register for the USABO with another school' if their own is not participating, via a 'My school is not participating' feature — 'there is no guarantee that a host school will be identified.'
cost_verbatim: 'the registration fee of $125... Payment is due no later than October 23, 2026'
cost_note: Fee is per SCHOOL, not per student — same institutional-cost pattern as HMMT and CMIMC. Should not be stored as a per-student cost.
INTERNATIONAL_ELIGIBILITY_CLAIM_NOT_CONF: A search result claimed international students may sit the Open Exam for a certificate but cannot advance, restricted to 'U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents' beyond that. I could NOT find this stated on usabo-trc.org's own Guidelines & Eligibility page or FAQ — neither page mentions 'international', 'citizen', or 'outside the US' at all in the text I retrieved. Per this lane's discipline, an aggregator claim that the primary source does not state is NOT recorded as fact. HOLD.
progression: Open Exam -> Semifinal -> National Finals (20 finalists) -> USA Biolympiad Team of 4 sent to IBO. '2027 International Biology Olympiad will be held in Warsaw, Poland, July 18 to 25, 2027.'
track_record: 'every member of the "USA Biolympiad Team" has continued to medal at the IBO' since CEE began administering it; #1 in the world 2007, 2011, 2013, 2024.
scale: 'enriches the life science education of nearly 12,000 talented students annually'
deadline_note: School registration/payment deadline, not a student deadline — same ownership issue as CR1-157's pattern.
classification_reason: Held at C_INCOMPLETE specifically because the one fact that would determine whether this is usable for ORYN's international audience — can a non-US student sit even the Open Exam — is not confirmed from the operator's own site. Publishing this as decision-grade without that would repeat the exact error this lane exists to prevent.
unresolved: Whether international/non-US students may register at all, even for the Open Exam only.
Whether the $125 fee is what a school actually charges students, or absorbed by the school.

organization: Taiwan Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education); executed by the Department of Architecture, National Taiwan University of Science and Technology (NTUST)
why_this_fills_a_measured_gap: CR1-152 measured Design at 2 actionable rows — the same tier as Law before Blackstone and Psychology before Brain Bee/IPsyO. This is a government-run, worldwide, no-fee, large-prize design competition and it was absent.
government_provenance_verbatim: 'Since 2003, the Ministry of Education (MOE) has been utilizing existing resources in schools to nurture young talents in the fields of arts and design.' Run 'From 2010' as successor to 2008-2009 pilot editions. Executed by NTUST's Department of Architecture.
eligibility_verbatim: 'Students currently enrolled in high school or above (under 30 years old)'
eligibility_note: 'High school or above' — the competition is NOT restricted to secondary students, but explicitly INCLUDES them, unlike most design competitions in this space which are university-only. Age cap 30 is generous and irrelevant for ORYN's 14-18 band.
eligible_countries: WORLDWIDE IN PRACTICE, NOT AN EXPLICIT RULE
eligible_countries_evidence: Official published statistics table, 2008-2025, showing 'Countries' and 'International Entries %' columns every year. **2025: 73 countries, 1,029 schools, 16,329 entries, of which international entries were the majority (per the international/Taiwan entries split shown for each year).** Brochure is offered in EIGHT languages including Arabic, Korean and Japanese. This is strong PARTICIPATION evidence, not a quoted eligibility sentence — I looked for and did not find an explicit 'open to all countries' statement. Recorded per the placement discipline: eligible_countries is NOT set to a plain 'worldwide', but the evidence is unusually strong for an implied-worldwide case, stronger than the Blue Ocean/Earth Prize participation counts I declined to promote earlier tonight.
track_record_table_excerpt: 2016: 69 countries, 14,864 entries. 2020: 64 countries, 20,377 entries (pandemic year — competition continued). 2025: 73 countries, 16,329 entries. Eighteen consecutive years of operation with published, year-by-year country counts — the most substantial published track record found in this entire lane.
category_note: Five distinct tracks. A student strong in visual/digital work has as much a route here as one interested in architecture — broader than most single-discipline design competitions.

2026_cycle.prizes: 'top prize of NTD 400,000' (~USD 13,000); 'total prize pool of NTD 4 million (USD 130,000)'

deadline_note: 2026 cycle dates (27 Apr - 6 Jul 2026) are known but that page was headed 'Call for Entries Coming Soon', so treating as not-yet-open rather than open. Re-check closer to April.
team_size: NOT STATED on the pages retrieved.
confidence_note: High on cost, categories, eligibility, and the participation track record. Medium on the explicit country-eligibility rule, which is inferred from 18 years of published statistics rather than a quoted sentence — flagged accordingly.
unresolved: Exact 2026 opening date beyond the submission window already published.

organization: NOT STATED on the pages retrieved (widely known to be a Boeing/miniPCR bio/ISS National Lab partnership, but I did not confirm this from an official page and am not asserting it)
secondary_character: genuine research — students design an original space-biotechnology experiment; winners fly it to the ISS
SEARCH_FRAMED_THIS_AS_WORLDWIDE_IT_IS_NO: The search summary that surfaced this candidate described it as available to 'teens worldwide'. **The operator's own contest page is unambiguous: 'Genes in Space gives U.S. students in grades 7-12 the chance to dream big and design a biotechnology experiment for space.'** US only. Caught before writing a worldwide claim — the same discipline that caught the LGIC non-finding and the Clark Scholars aggregator error.
advisor_note: Notably permissive — a PARENT can serve as the required adult sponsor, not only a teacher or mentor. Lower institutional barrier than most competitions requiring a school-affiliated advisor.
prize: Winning experiments are actually flown to and run aboard the International Space Station — the page references 'Genes in Space 13' as the current mission number, implying a long-running, credible track record (13 prior winning experiments launched).
deadline_note: That is an OPENING date, not a closing one — the page gives no closing deadline. Do not record 2026-01-05 as an application deadline.
recommendation: Add, but strictly gated to US students. Genuinely excellent for the ORYN users it fits — real research, real spaceflight, low barrier (parent can sponsor, no experience required) — but must never surface for a Turkish or other non-US student. Worth having precisely because it is well-verified rather than left as an unchecked aggregator claim.

organization: Beckman Biology Olympiad — a student-run high school club; originally created by OC Biology in 2021
provenance_caution: STUDENT-ORGANISED, NOT INSTITUTIONAL. This is run by a high school club (Beckman Biology Olympiad), hosted on a free Wix site, descended from another club's 2021 competition. That is a materially different tier of credibility from a university, ministry, or established foundation. Not dismissed on that basis — many genuinely useful, well-run things are student-organised — but it must not be presented to a student with the same weight as IBO, USABO, or TISDC. Same honesty standard applied to Blackstone Law Review (private LLC, no institutional affiliation, CR1-151) and Marshall Society (Cambridge relationship unstated, CR1-154).
eligibility_verbatim: 'All high schoolers (or equivalent age groups worldwide) are eligible to participate.'
eligibility_note: Placed directly as the eligibility statement itself — meets the placement test despite the organiser's small scale.
cost_verbatim: 'The competition will be entirely online and will be free of charge.'
format_verbatim: 'an individual multiple-choice exam and a team Biology Bowl'
format_note: A knowledge competition, NOT original research — testing cell biology, genetics, evolution, plants, animals, ethology and ecology. Should not be classified as a research opportunity; it belongs alongside USACO/AMC as a knowledge-competition rather than with CrowdMath/RSI as a research one.
deadline_note: 2027 dates not yet published; the organiser runs a mailing list for registration-opening notifications rather than a published future date. Do not infer one.
team_size: NOT STATED — the page describes an individual exam AND a team Biology Bowl without stating team size for the latter.
why_still_worth_recording: Free, worldwide, online, no institutional gatekeeping (no school registration needed, unlike USABO/AMC/HMMT). For a student with no school biology programme and no national olympiad access, this is a genuinely low-barrier entry point — the trade-off being lower external prestige.
confidence_note: Medium specifically because of organiser scale and stability — a single-club competition is more likely to lapse than an institutional one (compare ISSYP, CR1-140). Verify it is still running before any given cycle.

age_rule_verbatim: 'Participants are limited to students between 14-18 years old.'
age_note: EXACT MATCH to ORYN's stated 14-18 target band — not 13-19, not 'high school', but precisely this range, stated by the operator.

team_rule_verbatim: 'Each team must consist of between three to five students, ages 14 to 18 years, along with one adult technical mentor/coach and one team organizer.'
scale_verbatim: 'students from 190+ countries will unite in Incheon, Republic of Korea'

2026_event.theme: 'Igniting Innovation' — wildfire prevention, mitigation and recovery robotics challenge

theme_note: The annual theme is explicitly tied to one of the '14 Grand Challenges for Engineering' and a real-world problem (this year, wildfire resilience) — genuine applied-engineering content, not an abstract robotics drill.
TURKIYE_PRESENCE_CONFIRMED: Türkiye appears by name on FIRST Global's own interactive country map of national teams — confirmed present among 190+ listed countries. The map does not surface a specific organisation name in the text extracted this pass; a student would need to open Türkiye's specific team page (reached via the map) for the national partner's contact.
identity_caution: Türkmenistan again appears immediately after Türkiye in the alphabetical country list on the same map. Same adjacent-country pattern documented repeatedly tonight — noted for completeness, not because it caused an error here.
cost_note: NOT STATED on the pages retrieved. FIRST Global events historically involve real travel costs to the host country; do not record as free.
materials_accessibility: Game manuals and videos are provided in English, Arabic, Spanish, French and Portuguese — genuine multilingual accessibility, though Turkish is not among them.
unresolved: Türkiye's specific national partner organisation/contact — reachable via the team map but not extracted this pass.
Whether Türkiye's team has competed continuously or intermittently — presence on the map is not the same as active participation this cycle (per the IJSO lesson, CR1-079).

organization: NOT STATED on either page retrieved
why_this_fills_a_measured_gap: CR1-152 measured Environmental Science at 3. Free, worldwide, online, individual entry — the same shape that made IPsyO and CrowdMath valuable additions tonight.
STRUCTURAL_TWIN_OF_IPSYO: This competition's structure is line-for-line identical to IPsyO (CR1-153), researched earlier tonight: 'Global Grand Test' qualification (individual, multiple-choice, continent-timezone scheduling in the same three blocks: Asia&Oceania/Europe&Africa/North&South America) -> 'International Final' -> School Team Awards requiring 6+ students with top-6 scoring. Same phrasing, same mechanics, same advisor-verification requirement. This is either the same organiser running a family of subject-branded olympiads, or two organisers copying the same template. NEITHER page names an organiser, so I cannot confirm which — flagging the pattern rather than asserting a shared operator.
THE_STALE_BANNER_PATTERN_A_THIRD_TIME: The homepage's call-to-action still reads 'Register for IEnvO 2026' with a Global Grand Test date of **August 8, 2026 — 15 days in the PAST** at retrieval. The dedicated current-cycle page states plainly: 'Registration for IEnvO 2026 has closed.' Same shape as Özyeğin's stale 'APPLICATIONS ARE NOW OPENED' banner (CR1-020) and IPsyO's own landing-page staleness that I initially got wrong (CR1-153's self-correction). **The lesson holds a third time: trust the dedicated current-cycle page, not the homepage CTA.**
cycle_status_evidence: 'Registration for IEnvO 2026 has closed.' (current-cycle page, authoritative) vs. stale 'Register for IEnvO 2026' CTA (homepage, not authoritative).
eligibility_verbatim: 'Grades 9-12'; 'Currently enrolled high school students'; 'Students graduating in 2027 or later'
eligibility_note: Identical graduating-year exclusion logic to IPsyO — bars the class that just graduated.
eligible_countries: '50+ Countries' / '10K+ Students' stated as participation stats on the homepage; the current-cycle page describes the Global Grand Test as scheduled across three continental time-zone blocks, which only makes sense for genuinely global participation. Recorded as WORLDWIDE on the strength of the operational (timezone-block) evidence, not the bare stat.
advisor_requirement_verbatim: 'School or institutional advisor support' listed as a requirement; 'Your advisor will register you through the official IEnvO website.'
learning_areas: Land (soil science, land use, terrestrial conservation)
Human Activity (sustainable development, environmental policy, green technology)
learning_areas_note: Five domains spanning hard science through POLICY ('environmental policy, green technology' under Human Activity) — relevant to both a Environmental Science-interested student and a Politics/Public-Policy one.
team_awards_verbatim: For School Team Awards, '6 or more students' from a school are required for eligibility, with 'top 6 students' scores' counted in team scoring.
cost_note: NOT STATED on either page retrieved.
deadline_note: 2026 cycle closed; no 2027 dates published yet. Flag for re-check, same as IPsyO.
confidence_note: High on structure and eligibility. The unnamed organiser and unconfirmed relationship to IPsyO's operator are the open threads.
unresolved: Organising body's name — not stated on either page.
Whether this shares an operator with IPsyO.
